output.title: Address Resolution Protocol
output.description: The Address Resolution Protocol (ARP) is used to map a network layer address (protocol address) to a link layer address (hardware address), such as MAC addresses. This document describes the structure of ARP packets, their usage, and related considerations for implementation and monitoring.

content_sections.description: ARP defines several fields in its packet format:

fields.description: Length of hardware address in bytes
Length of protocol address in bytes
Target's hardware address (not used in request)

details: The sender hardware and protocol addresses are mandatory to build translation tables.
The target hardware address has no meaning in request packets but is the requester's hardware address in reply packets.
The packet uses Ethernet byte order (big-endian) for defined fields.

content_sections.description: ARP can be used to monitor network activity without knowing higher-level protocols:
process_steps: Monitor records <protocol type, sender protocol address, sender hardware address> in a table.
Length fields indicate hardware/protocol addresses lengths.
For reply packets: discard if opcode is REPLY and target matches the monitor's address.
For request packets: respond with REPLY if target matches monitor's address.
important_note: Monitors don't need to know specific protocol mappings, only the lengths for parsing addresses.
Monitoring can help diagnose ARP issues without understanding higher-layer protocols.

content_sections.description: Demonstrates ARP in a simple Ethernet network scenario:

scenario.context: Host X wants to send Internet packet to host Y
actions: X creates an ARPPacket with opcode=REQUEST for IP=Y
X broadcasts request to all hosts on cable
Y receives and responds with ARPPacket of opcode=REPLY
X receives reply and updates its ARP table

scenario.result: Both machines now have ARP mappings allowing direct communication via Ethernet.

details: Moving hosts may require stale entries to be cleared.
Rebooted hosts reset their tables, but other hosts might have old data.

solutions: Daemon-initiated revalidation: send REQUEST to verify address
Timeout-based entry deletion: remove entries after inactivity

key_points: ARP enables mapping between MAC addresses and IP addresses on Ethernet networks.
It's designed for broadcast media like Ethernet where multiple hosts share the same physical network.
The protocol supports both request/reply functionality with opcode fields.
